descriptionChirho: The proper noun 'Atalyah(u) refers primarily to the queen mother of Judah (daughter/granddaughter of Omri and Ahab), who seized the throne after her son Ahaziah's death and ruled for six years until overthrown by Jehoiada the priest. A secondary referent is a Benjamite (1 Chr 8:26) and a returnee (Ezra 8:7), but the name is identical. All four clusters represent the same name with conjunctive waw and minor spelling variation (Atalyah/Atalyahu). Multilingual glosses confirm unity: Spanish 'Atalia', Hindi 'Atalyah/Atalyahu', Arabic 'Athalyaa/Atalya', Korean 'Adallya/Adalryat', and Swahili 'Athalia' throughout.
